title: Sets and Maps
learningObjectives: Explain sets and maps and use the relevant JavaScript language feature correctly.

understand.concept: Set stores unique values and preserves insertion order. Map stores key-value entries and allows keys of any value type. Both provide methods such as add/set, has, delete, clear, and iteration.
understand.whyItMatters: Set is useful for uniqueness checks; Map is useful when keys are not limited to strings. They often express intent more clearly than arrays or plain objects for these jobs.
understand.analogy: A Set is a collection that refuses duplicate entries; a Map is a labelled collection where each key points to a value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript language protocols, primitive identity, and date/time semantics are defined by the language and runtime.

explain.narrative: The Set contains each tag once. The Map retrieves a score using its key.

examples.explanation: The Set contains each tag once. The Map retrieves a score using its key.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the behaviour described in the lesson.

practise.guidedTask: Create a Set of unique course tags and a Map of learner names to scores. Test has(), delete(), and iteration.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that uses this feature with normal inputs and edge cases. Explain when this feature is preferable to a simpler alternative.
hints: Read the return value and iteration protocol carefully.
Test duplicate, invalid, and boundary values.
Avoid assuming locale or time-zone output is identical everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which collection type stores unique values?
questions.explanation: Set stores unique values and ignores duplicate additions.
